2022_07_5_d_fy23_proposed_budget_complet.paragraph: Oakland Schools, the Oakland County intermediate school district, brought its FY2022-23 original budget, budget assumptions and five-year forecasts to the Board of Education as agenda item 5.D. on May 17, 2022, with every schedule dated March 2022 and stamped 03.24.22. Enterprise-wide funding is budgeted at $391.2 million against $393.2 million of expenditures, with property taxes of $216.6 million rising 4.0% and an eighth consecutive Headlee rollback assumed. The single largest use of resources is $174.4 million of transfers to local districts and other funds, anchored by a PA-18 special education base distribution to LEAs budgeted at $148,300,000.

## Entity and document
Oakland Schools, one of 56 Michigan intermediate school districts (established 1962), presented item 5.D., "FY23 Proposed Budget Complete Doc," at the May 17, 2022 Board meeting. Contents: the Enterprise Wide Executive Summary & Budget Assumptions (March 2022), General Education, Special Education and Career Focused Education fund budgets with five-year forecasts, other funds, the 5-Year Capital Outlay Plan, and Annual Budgeting Amendment Reports OSBG0014A / OSBG0014 run as of 3/24/2022 by user STYMAD - Dawn Styma. Pages carry the footer "FY23 Proposed Budget" and date stamp 03.24.22.

## Property taxes
Budgeted tax revenue moves from $208,277,600 to $216,608,800, an $8,331,200 or 4.00% increase: General Education $12,869,900, Special Education $163,694,800, Career Focused Education $40,044,100. Oakland County taxable values are expected to rise more than 6.25%, yet the budget assumes an eighth consecutive Headlee rollback. Tax revenues are up 27% since 2014 but remain $8.7 million below pre-recession levels; the Great Recession cost 24.5% of county taxable valuation and $438.5 million of district revenue through fiscal year 2022. The Michigan Tax Tribunal reserve is .25% of tax revenues, about $536,300; $12.9 million has been repaid over eleven years.

## Personnel and benefits
A 2% across-the-board increase applies, with non-union step growth of 1.28% and union wage base growth of .98%. Eight MPSERS rates are in effect; Basic/MIP with Health Care Premium Subsidy is 28.23% through September 30, 2022, and the blended rate is 28.26%. The UAAL stabilization rate is proposed to rise from 15.05% to 16.65%. Health care hard caps move to $20,658.54 (family), $15,841.22 (individual plus one) and $7,574.78 (single) on projected medical CPI of 3.7%. Total staffing goes 653.96, 660.31 and 665.41 across the three years, a change of 5.10 FTE.

## Transfers, capital and forecast
Other financing uses run $175,574,800 to $174,384,400, dominated by the PA-18 base distribution of $148,300,000. Capital outlay rises from $5,182,200 to $6,628,800; debt service from $3,020,400 to $3,391,700, principal up $420,000 on the 2016 Refunding Bonds; grant revenue falls to $106,979,900. Policy 3230 subsidies total $1,211,750. Taxes are forecast to grow 4.0%, 3.25%, then 3.0% through 2027-28; General Education unassigned balance is forecast at $4.3 million (18.2%) in 2023-24 down to $3.3 million (13.0%) in 2026-27 and $3.7 million (14.9%) in 2027-28.

## Identity, governance and document mechanics
Oakland Schools is an autonomous, tax-supported public school district and one of 56 intermediate school districts in Michigan, established in 1962 and governed under Michigan General School Law. The budget book -- agenda item 5.D., "FY23 Proposed Budget Complete Doc," meeting date May 17, 2022 -- carries the cover "Enterprise Wide Executive Summary & Budget Assumptions - Original Budget - March 2022 - Fiscal Year 2022-23," is footed "FY23 Proposed Budget" and stamped 03.24.22. Embedded system reports are OSBG0014A "Proposed Budget Comparison" (by function) and OSBG0014 (by location and by object), run 03/24/2022 by user STYMAD - Dawn Styma. Budgetary authority rests in Board Policies 3050, 3100 (contingency appropriation; amendments at least three times each fiscal year), 3150 (fund balance targets, with the General Education unassigned range reaching 7.5% to 12.5% in FY 2022-23) and 3170 (line-item transfers within a fund; inter-fund transfers need prior Board approval); subsidy reporting is required by Policy 3230. Statutes cited include the General Property Tax Act, Public Act 206 of 1893 (MCL 211.24e); the Uniform Budgeting and Accounting Act, Public Act 2 of 1968; and the Revised School Code, Public Act 451 of 1976 (MCL 380.624 and MCL 380.684, the latter as amended by Public Act 45 of 2007), with Bulletin 1022 as mandatory guide. The proposed budget must go to each constituent district no later than May 1 and be adopted no later than June 30.

## Enterprise-wide sources and uses
Total FY2022-23 funding is $391.2 million: property taxes $216.6 million; other local and investment revenue $36.9 million; state source revenue $21.6 million; other financing sources and indirect revenue $9.1 million; estimated new grant award funding $84.2 million; estimated grant carryover funding $22.8 million. Total expenditures are $393.2 million: salary, wage and benefits $80.4 million; purchased services, supplies, dues and fees $20.5 million; electric and natural gas utilities $.9 million; capital outlay $6.6 million; transfers to LEAs and other funds $174.4 million; grant related expenditures $107.0 million; payment on existing debt $3.4 million. Both figures are net of eligible inter-company eliminated Risk Related Activity Fund amounts.

## Property taxes and the tax environment
Property tax revenue is budgeted to increase 4.0%, or $5.5 million, on Oakland County Equalization Division projections of taxable value growth of more than 6.25%, offset by an assumed Headlee rollback -- the eighth year in a row. By fund: General Education $12,374,900 to $12,869,900; Special Education $157,398,800 to $163,694,800; Career Focused Education $38,503,900 to $40,044,100; total $208,277,600 to $216,608,800, a change of $8,331,200 or 4.00%. Tax base composition is 70% principal residence and 30% non-principal residence. Tax revenues are up 27% since 2014 yet $8.7 million below pre-recession levels as of FY2021-22; the Great Recession produced a 24.5% cumulative loss in county taxable valuations over four declining years and $438.5 million of cumulative district revenue erosion through fiscal year 2022. Tax abatements peaked in fiscal years 2012 and 2013. Michigan Tax Tribunal judgments have cost $12.9 million over the past eleven years; the FY2022-23 MTT reserve is .25% of tax revenues, about $536,300 in expense.

## General Education Fund (Fund 100)
Beginning fund equity is $5,259,000 (non-spendable prepaids $14,300; assigned $435,000; unassigned $4,809,700). Revenue of $22,932,400 comprises local sources $15,732,000, state sources $6,406,100 and other financing sources $794,300; property taxes are 56% of total revenue. Expenditures of $23,544,000 break out as General Administration $2,037,400, Finance and Operations $9,070,000, Instructional Services $9,442,600 and Plant and Fixed Charges $2,994,000, producing a planned operating deficit of $(611,600) and ending equity of $4,647,400 (unassigned $4,633,100; the narrative separately states an unassigned balance of $4,547,800). Notable revenue lines: Section 81 ISD Operations $4,058,400 to $4,139,600 (the Governor's budget included a 5% increase; 2% is budgeted); Section 147c MPSERS UAAL Rate Stabilization $1,841,600 to $2,030,000; Section 147a Normal Cost Offset $55,400; State Payment in Lieu of Taxes $152,100; Illuminate $190,600 to $555,000 as the base-product subsidy returns from 100% to 50%; workshop fees $100,000 to $175,000; CTN $384,600 to $334,400. Department 046 Technology Services Audio/Visual Support is combined into 030 Technical Support Services and department 022 Communications Video Production into 049 Communication Services, both zeroed in FY23. Fund 100 expense by function includes Improve of Instruction $7,238,400, Support Svcs Tech $5,631,500 and Exec Administration $1,663,000. Forecast assumptions include capital outlay of $1,238,000 for 2023-24 through 2026-27 and $238,000 in 2027-28, purchased services growth of 2%, supplies and dues growth of 1.0%, medical CPI of 3.5%, and unassigned balances of $4.3 million (18.2%), $4.1 million (16.8%), $3.8 million (15.1%), $3.3 million (13.0%) and $3.7 million (14.9%).

## Special Education Fund (Fund 200) and PA-18
Revenues total $171,956,400 (property tax $163,694,800; investment $52,500; fee based $100,000; state $5,869,200; state payment in lieu of taxes $1,934,400; other financing sources $305,500) against expenditures of $171,894,000, an operating excess of $62,400. Ending fund balance is $11,520,000, holding $10,419,600 restricted for future center facility renovations, $27,000 non-spendable and $1,073,400 restricted for special education, equal to 5.00% of expenditures net of LEA transfers. The PA-18 base distribution to local districts is $148,300,000, budgeted to increase about $7.9 million or 5.6%, and is forecast to reach $175,141,500 by 2027-28; LEA support transfers are $2,700,000 and the additional distribution line goes to zero from $7,403,700. Program subsidies location 078 totals $151,000,000 against $150,493,500. FY23 district distributions include Bloomfield Hills $11,668,800, Walled Lake $11,560,000, Rochester $11,325,800, Birmingham $10,095,200, Farmington $9,339,900, Waterford $8,523,700, Troy $7,998,100, Hazel Park $7,740,800 and Public School Academies $1,607,100. Special Populations serves approximately 21,185 students with an Individualized Education Program.

## Career Focused Education Fund (Fund 600, "Vocational Ed Fund")
Revenue is $46,269,300 (local $40,411,100, state $5,730,900, other financing $127,300) and expenditures $46,259,100, a surplus of $10,200; ending equity is $5,825,500 (restricted $5,814,900, non-spendable $10,600). Property taxes of $40.0 million are 87% of total revenue. State lines include Voc Ed Sec 61a.1 falling from $2,102,600 to $1,735,000 (-17.48%), Sec 61a.2 $13,800, CTE Early/Middle College 61b $244,600, Section 147c $2,851,800 to $3,150,000, and State Payment in Lieu of Taxes $473,300; Wayne RESA pays $25,000 for Section 107 Adult Education monitoring. Expenditures split into CFE Campus and Other Program Operations $27,255,700, LEA Transfers and Program Subsidies $5,484,000, and CFE Plant and Fixed Charges $13,519,400. Nineteen CTE programs are listed (codes 501 through 597, including Cosmetology 531, Cyber Security 548, Mechatronics 575 and Health Sciences 580). The four Oakland Schools Technical Campuses, serving approximately 2,700 students from all 28 constituent districts, total $5,469,300 (NW), $5,576,500 (SE), $6,162,700 (NE) and $6,006,400 (SW), with total campus operations of $23,214,900. Forecast commitments include $3.6 million annually for Support to LEAs Regional Programs, $1.8 million for transportation reimbursement, $543,700 for STEM mobile classroom operating costs, transfers out to debt service of $2.3 million per year, and annual debt service payments of $2.5 million through 2036. Restricted fund balance is forecast at $6.3 million (13.2%) rising to $8.1 million (15.4%).

## Cost allocation
The general allocation splits 50% General Education / 25% Special Education / 25% Career Focused Education; activity-based FTE allocation is 24/24/52; space utilization 50/24/26; transportation miles 73/25/2; Technology Services Licensing 70/15/15; Financial Services property taxes 6/75.5/18.5. The Special Education Fund carries a 25% maximum allocation cap on each eligible function-based cost pool. Allocated departments total $11,406,200 (Fund 100), $6,555,300 (Fund 200) and $8,282,600 (Fund 600), a grand total of $26,244,100 or 11.61%.

## Personnel, retirement and insurance
A 2% across-the-board increase applies, with non-union step growth of 1.28% and union wage base growth of .98%. FICA is 7.65%, with social security of 6.2% on wages up to $147,000 for calendar year 2022. Eight MPSERS rates run October 1, 2021 through September 30, 2022, with payroll rates of 28.23%, 25.31%, 24.45%, 20.96%, 21.82%, 20.96%, 27.37% and 27.16% plus a 15.05% UAAL stabilization rate; the blended rate exclusive of UAAL is 28.26%, projected to increase 1.0% annually. Hard caps rise to $20,658.54 (family), $15,841.22 (individual plus one) and $7,574.78 (single) on 3.7% medical CPI, with employees contributing approximately 14% on average. Salaries and wages with FICA total $46,836,800 to $51,131,200 (9.2%); MPSERS retirement $20,092,500 to $20,758,300; healthcare insurance $6,355,400 to $6,486,200; other insurances $2,296,500 to $1,987,700; utilities $905,700 to $937,500 (Constellation Energy Services); purchased services, supplies and dues less utilities $21,334,700 to $20,477,900. The district belongs to the SET-SEG Self-Insurers Workers' Compensation Fund and moved dental and vision to premium-based plans effective January 1, 2022. New positions include a 1.0 FTE Recruiting Manager, a .33 FTE part-time Controller, 2.0 FTE in Technology Services (Business Support Specialist and Associate Business Analyst), 2.0 FTE Campus Bookkeepers and a .10 FTE Psychologist increase, offset by a .33 FTE Administration decrease; total staffing moves 653.96, 660.31, 665.41, a change of 5.10.

## Programs, subsidies and collaborations
Cooperative service subsidies total $1,211,750: Xello $302,700; Illuminate DnA $363,800; Atlas Rubicon $184,500; Nepris $155,000; Discovery Education Streaming $149,500; PowerSchool BusinessPlus per pupil $17,400; CDX Automotive $15,000; Meltwater $14,850; Student Achievement Media $5,000; TV Eyes $2,400; Sprout Social $1,600. Literacy Essentials Oakland (LEO) is a five-year early literacy project launched in 2019-20 with up to $5 million from Oakland Schools. The HR/Finance Consortium, named Michigan Partnership for Essential Education Resources (MiPEER), covers twenty-two districts converting to PowerSchool BusinessPlus. Fee-based programs: VLAC K-8 at 500 FTE and $6,450 resident / $6,650 non-resident tuition; VLAC 9-12 at 100 FTE and $6,700 / $6,900; Accelerated College Experience (ACE) at 200 students and $4,900, offering up to 60 transferrable college credits with Oakland Community College. Medicaid Billing Services is expected to generate approximately $11.4 million of revenue for LEAs. Also cited: a $13.6 million Special Education center program renovation; 121 schools in the Michigan Green Schools Program; the county's loss of over 145,000 jobs to COVID-19 with roughly 60% recovered by the first quarter of 2021; Emerging Sectors investment of over $5.4 billion with almost 55,000 jobs created and over 40,300 retained as of December 2020; and the Oakland80 goal of 80% of adults holding a post-secondary credential by 2030. Oakland Schools received no ESSER, Governor's Emergency Education Relief or Coronavirus Relief Fund money, funding COVID costs from tax revenues and state aid, and supported the Oxford School District crisis with mental health consultants, psychologists and social workers.

## Other funds, debt and capital
Funds presented include 105, 205 and 605 funded projects, 270 Shared Services and Tuition Programs, 271 ONE, 273 Medicaid, 277 HR/Finance Consortium, 290 School Activities, 311 (2016 Refunding Bonds), 313 and 314 (2010 QSCB), 404 CFE Campus Renovations, 406 Administration Building Renovations, 409 Career Connections Facility, 710 Production Printing Enterprise and 810 Risk Related Activity. Debt service principal rises $420,000 to $1,395,000 with interest of $1,996,700, total $3,391,700. Grant revenue falls to $106,979,900 (local $1,335,600; state $39,379,700; federal $66,264,600). The 5-Year Capital Outlay Plan, presented for first reading on March 24, 2022, shows grand totals of $9,229,600 for 2024, $8,874,800 for 2025, $3,876,000 for 2026 and $6,669,800 for 2027, with a grand totals memo-only column of $38,279,400; the largest items are HVAC of $4,052,300 in 2025 (including $3,932,800 at the SE campus) and $2,491,700 in 2027, and roof repair and replacement of $1,118,100 in 2027.
